title: Three Years and One Short Stone
subtitle: 文化遗产 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）
meta: 主题语境：文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）　|　核心词汇：memorial　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 memorial 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the guardian ① built the memorial that no visitor in the garden would have recorded, and he said the building was the whole of the year. The ② memorial, meaning the monument itself and not the stone, ran three years and stayed unrecorded in the book; a memorial, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ memorial in that garden had the same short stone beside it, and the ④ memorial at the far wall, meaning the name they kept for the children to read and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A memorial, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the guardian said the recording is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the memorial was the whole of the matter, meaning the memory and not the monument. The ⑥ memorial, meaning the memory and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; memorial, he said, is either something you build or the only word that means both a monument and a memory. He said the memory is the part they remember.

By 1959 the ⑦ memorial had become a line in an inscription, and the inscription had become an argument about the short stone. The ⑧ memorial of the whole thing, the guardian wrote in November, was one garden and three years of recording; memorial, he said, is either the name at the far wall or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ memorial I remember is the monument recorded in the inscription, which closed in 1961 and is still recorded as the quietest in the garden. A ⑩ memorial, my mother said in 1963, is the only monument that improves by being recorded; every memorial, she said, is a memory that has agreed to look like a monument. She said the memory was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 纪念碑；纪念物（指纪念园里每一座旁边的那一座）
B. n. 纪念碑；纪念物（指那座纪念物本身，与石碑相对）
C. 固定搭配：build the memorial 修建这座纪念碑
D. n. 纪念碑；纪念物（指留给孩子们读的那一个名字那一座）
E. n. 立碑之事（抽象总称，指一处纪念园的纪念碑之事）
F. n. 纪念碑；纪念物（指碑文里写到、被记载的的那一座）
G. n. 纪念、追思（指一件事里人人都记却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 追思（抽象总称，指人人都记却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: built the memorial that no visitor in the garden would have recorded
The memorial, meaning the monument itself and not the stone
the memorial at the far wall
the memorial was the whole of the matter
the memorial had become a line in an inscription
The memorial of the whole thing
A memorial, my mother said in 1963

answers.why: build the memorial 意为“修建这座纪念碑”，1954 年那位守祠人把纪念园里没有一位来访者肯记载的一座纪念碑做了一遍。
memorial 意为“纪念碑；纪念物”，指那座纪念物本身而不是石碑，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被记载。
memorial 意为“纪念碑；纪念物”，指纪念园里每一座旁边的那一座，每一座旁边都有同一块小小的石碑。
memorial 意为“纪念碑；纪念物”，指最远那面纪念墙留给孩子们读的那一个名字那一座，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
memorial 意为“纪念、追思”，指一件事里人人都记却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份纪念就是那件事的全部。
memorial 意为“追思”，指人人都记却无人提起的那样东西而不是那座纪念物，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
memorial 意为“纪念碑；纪念物”，指碑文里写到、被记载的的那一座，到 1959 年这一座成了碑文里的一行。
memorial 意为“立碑之事”，守祠人十一月写道，整件事的纪念碑之事是一处纪念园和三个年头的记载。
memorial 意为“纪念碑；纪念物”，我记得的是碑文里记载过的那一座，1961 年立成了，至今仍被说成纪念园里最安静的一座。
memorial 为抽象总称，母亲 1963 年说，纪念碑是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的纪念物。
